newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel disrupted by three-hour French strike.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel disrupted by three-hour French strike.

text.p: French strikers blocked tourist and truck traffic through the Channel Tunnel linking France and Britain for three hours on Wednesday in a protest at working conditions.
Drivers sat in their vehicles in stifling sunlight as the stoppage, the first major action by unions at Eurotunnel, created tailbacks several km (miles) long at the French terminal.

Most of those trapped were British and Dutch tourists. Some of them argued bitterly with the strikers, accusing them of taking passengers hostage by preventing them from loading onto Shuttle trains to travel through the subsea link.

No Shuttles left Coquelles during the strike and only one train carrying trucks departed. At the British end of the Channel Tunnel at Folkestone, Shuttle services were running late and dwindled to just one departure every hour.
French strikers lifted pickets at toll booths at around 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) after winning a management promise of talks to review working conditions.
Officials estimated that only about 100 workers heeded the strike call. Eurotunnel employs just over 3,000 staff, including 1,600 French workers.
Freight traffic and Eurostar passenger trains, run by the state railways SNCF, were not hit by the action.
Management and unions later met to discuss workers' demands for better working conditions and charges by staff that management have ignored grievances over salaries and working hours.
"We're proposing to meet again on July 29," Eurotunnel director-general Georges-Christian Chazot told Reuters after the meeting. Unions declined to respond immediately to the offer of new talks.
One of the workers' 22 demands is for overtime pay to start immediately after the end of a shift. Currently, workers have to stay on at least 30 minutes extra to qualify for overtime.
